## Notification estate full-scope assessment, 2026-09-09

A record, not a task list. It is counted here because its ten findings are real outstanding work that appears in no register, not because the file should become one. Ten, not the nine a hand count first reported — F-10 sits below the visible run of F-01 to F-09, which is the ordinary way a hand count goes wrong and the reason this one is read by a pattern.

> **Every entry counts as open.** An audit is a record of what was true on its date and is never edited to agree with the present — the rule docs/audits/ already lives by. So nothing in it can be marked closed in place. Its findings are counted as outstanding until an item in another source supersedes them, and none does yet. F-02 records a partial correction inline and its governance half is stated as open.

## Flow-truth persistence review

A record. Includes two security findings, S1 and S2, which is why leaving them uncounted mattered.

> **Every entry counts as open.** A record is not edited to agree with the present, so no finding is ever closed in place. Until 2026-09-15 that meant all 29 stayed counted open: the rebuilt DGO_FLOW_TRUTH_PERSISTENCE package answered most of them, but tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs asserted no finding by id, so nothing established WHICH. 13 documents are register-shaped and are not places work hides — they restate a
counted source, or they are records whose live findings have since been taken up elsewhere. They
are listed rather than quietly exempted, because a judgement on the record can be disagreed with
and a silent exemption cannot.

| Document | Why it is not counted |
|---|---|
| [`GOVERNANCE-STATUS.md`](../../docs/deployment/governance/GOVERNANCE-STATUS.md) | Generated from governance-estate-position.json, which IS counted. Counting it too would double every governance finding. |
| [`WHAT-WAS-DONE.md`](../../docs/deployment/governance/WHAT-WAS-DONE.md) | A narrative of the same position file. Counted there. |
| [`AGENT_COMMISSIONING_DIRECTIVE.md`](../../docs/deployment/AGENT_COMMISSIONING_DIRECTIVE.md) | Cites the readiness register's items to brief an agent. Every id in it is counted there. |
| [`COMMISSIONING_AGENT_BRIEF.md`](../../docs/deployment/COMMISSIONING_AGENT_BRIEF.md) | Its O-1 to O-4 are the four conditions for production, each discharged by readiness register items that are counted. The O- ids are a framing, not a backlog. |
| [`OPERATOR_WALKTHROUGH.md`](../../docs/deployment/OPERATOR_WALKTHROUGH.md) | A reading of 2026-08-31, superseded on status and banner-marked as such. Every item it names is in the readiness register. |
| [`EXECUTION-AGENT-BRIEF.md`](../../docs/deployment/governance/EXECUTION-AGENT-BRIEF.md) | WP-0 to WP-39 are work packages that decompose the governance runbook's steps. The work is counted as GOV findings; the packages are how it is handed to an agent. |
| [`EXPLICIT_EXECUTION_SPECIFICATION.md`](../../docs/deployment/live-operations-console/EXPLICIT_EXECUTION_SPECIFICATION.md) | OP-001 to OP-014 specify operations the console performs. A specification of what exists, not a list of what is outstanding. |
| [`CAPABILITY_ASSESSMENT_R11.6.md`](../../docs/audits/CAPABILITY_ASSESSMENT_R11.6.md) | Seven of its nine gaps were fixed and verified in 2026-08; the two that remain open, G-03 and G-04, are carried by the readiness register — G-04 as an item, G-03 as the rotation ITEM-22 closed. Counting them again would double them. |
| [`BRANCH_CONSOLIDATION_AUDIT_2026-09-05.md`](../../docs/audits/BRANCH_CONSOLIDATION_AUDIT_2026-09-05.md) | A record of the merge that produced this baseline. Its R- ids are recommendations about that merge, which has happened. |
| [`DESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF_ASSESSMENT.md`](../../docs/audits/DESIGN_AUDIT_BRIEF_ASSESSMENT.md) | Its live remnant is ITEM-57 in the readiness register — the archived design system, unreconciled, a decision for the agency. Counted there. |
| [`04-findings-recommendations.md`](../../docs/audits/repository-hygiene/04-findings-recommendations.md) | Assessed against commit c2d78ba2ea23 at 294 tracked files; this tree has 1,900. A record of a scope that no longer exists. |
| [`CLOSED.md`](../../docs/deployment/CLOSED.md) | Generated from the readiness register and the governance estate position, and it lists only what those two record as CLOSED. Counting it would double every discharged item and, worse, count closed work as outstanding — the exact inversion this estate spent a week correcting. It is register-shaped by construction, which is why it is declared here rather than exempted silently. |
| [`MASTER_REGISTER.md`](../../docs/deployment/MASTER_REGISTER.md) | Generated from every counted source in this file — it enumerates the same open items with what each one needs to close, and carries no item of its own. Counting it would double all 87. It is the most register-shaped document in the estate, which is exactly why it is declared rather than exempted: a document that reads as the master list is the most dangerous place for an uncounted item to appear. |

---

## What this does not tell you

It counts items, and items are not equal. One agency decision can gate more than ten provisioning
steps, and the flow-truth review's twenty-nine findings are against a single package. Read
[`ACTION_PLAN.md`](./ACTION_PLAN.md) for what to do next, in the order that unblocks the most;
this document exists to stop work hiding, not to prioritise it.

It also cannot tell you that a finding in a record has been overtaken. Audits are never edited to
agree with the present, so their findings stay counted until an item in a tracked source
supersedes them — which is the honest default, and occasionally an overcount.
